blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: A DaemonSet runs one copy of a Pod on every node. It comes from the apps/v1 API.
blocks.why: Node helpers, such as log collectors and monitoring agents, need to run everywhere.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create: a DaemonSet, from the apps/v1 API

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.what: This DaemonSet is called log-collector. Its Pods get names that start with it.
blocks.why: You use the name to check how many nodes it covers.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: A name to find the DaemonSet
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: log-collector

blocks.title: Which Pods belong to it?
blocks.what: The selector picks Pods labelled app: log-collector.
blocks.why: Its own label keeps it apart from app: web, so no Service sends web traffic here by accident.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because a DaemonSet must have a selector.
blocks.comment: Manage the Pods that carry this label
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: log-collector
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: log-collector

blocks.title: Describe the Pods
blocks.what: The template is the blueprint for each Pod. It gives each Pod the selector’s label.
blocks.why: The template labels must match the selector, as in a Deployment.
blocks.ifRemoved: The DaemonSet would have nothing to create, so Kubernetes rejects it.
blocks.comment: The blueprint for each Pod, with the label the selector looks for
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: log-collector
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: log-collector
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: log-collector

blocks.title: What should run?
blocks.what: A busybox container prints a message, then sleeps. A real collector would read the node’s log files.
blocks.why: There is no replicas field. The number of nodes decides how many Pods run.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the DaemonSet, because its Pods would have nothing to run.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: log-collector
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: log-collector
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: log-collector
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: collector
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "echo Collecting logs on $NODE_NAME && sleep 3600"]

blocks.title: Which node am I on?
blocks.what: NODE_NAME is filled in from the Pod’s own spec.nodeName, the node it was placed on.
blocks.why: Each copy can label its work with its node. The message proves one Pod runs per node.
blocks.ifRemoved: The message prints an empty node name. The Pods still run.
blocks.comment: Tell the container the name of its node
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: log-collector
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: log-collector
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: log-collector
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: collector
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "echo Collecting logs on $NODE_NAME && sleep 3600"]
          env:
            - name: NODE_NAME
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: spec.nodeName

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version that define this kind. DaemonSets are in apps/v1.
notes.kind: The type of object to create. A DaemonSet runs one Pod on every node.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.metadata.name: The DaemonSet’s name. Its Pods get names that start with it.
notes.spec: The desired state of the DaemonSet. There is no replicas field.
notes.spec.selector: Which Pods this DaemonSet manages. It cannot change after creation.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels: Pods must have all of these labels to be managed by this DaemonSet.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels.app: Match Pods whose app label is log-collector.
notes.spec.template: The Pod template: the blueprint for the Pod on each node.
notes.spec.template.metadata: Details given to every Pod created from the template.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels: Labels given to every Pod. They must match the selector.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels.app: Every Pod gets app: log-collector, its own label, so web Services never select it.
notes.spec.template.spec: What each Pod runs. This is the same spec as in a Pod file.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers: The containers in each Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].name: The container’s name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].image: A tiny image with basic shell tools, pinned to a version.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].command: Print which node this Pod runs on, then sleep for an hour.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[].va: Take the value from somewhere else instead of writing it here.
Take the value from a field of this Pod.
spec.nodeName: the node Kubernetes placed this Pod on.

tryIt.result: DESIRED, CURRENT, and READY all equal the number of nodes. A one-node practice cluster shows 1.
One Pod per node. The NODE column names a different node for each.
Each Pod prints Collecting logs on, followed by its node’s name.
Removes the DaemonSet and its Pods on every node.

questions.question: Why is there no replicas field?
answers: A DaemonSet runs one Pod on each node, so the node count decides
Replicas are set on the command line
questions.explain: A DaemonSet follows the nodes. Add a node and it gains a Pod.

questions.question: A new node joins the cluster. What happens?
answers: Nothing until you apply the file again
The DaemonSet starts a Pod on the new node
One Pod moves to the new node
questions.explain: The DaemonSet watches the nodes and starts a Pod on each new one by itself.

questions.question: Where does $NODE_NAME get its value?
answers: From the Pod’s own spec.nodeName, through fieldRef
You type it when you apply
questions.explain: fieldRef copies a field of the Pod into the variable. spec.nodeName is the node it runs on.

fix.message: The DaemonSet "log-collector" is invalid: spec.template.spec.containers[0].env[0].valueFrom.fieldRef.fieldPath: Invalid value: "spec.nodename": error converting fieldPath: field label not supported: spec.nodename
fix.explain: Field names are case-sensitive. nodename is not a Pod field, so Kubernetes cannot fill in the variable.
fix.fix: Write the field exactly: spec.nodeName, with a capital N.

sources.title: Expose Pod information to containers through environment variables
